svg.title: Timeline: how Ajinomoto Build-up Film came out of the MSG seasoning line
svg.desc: A vertical timeline on a single rail. The seasoning era, in coral: 1908, Kikunae Ikeda traces the taste of kombu broth to glutamic acid; 1909, AJI-NO-MOTO umami seasoning goes on sale, Ajinomoto crystallizing that glutamic acid into MSG; 1956, molasses and starch are fed to bacteria that excrete glutamic acid at scale, leaving co-products such as amino-acid-rich fermentation liquor and chlorinated paraffin. The rail changes color at a marker, and the semiconductor era continues in teal: 1970s, the Ajinomoto Group begins basic R&D on applications of amino acid chemistry to epoxy resins and their composites, and finds that chlorinated paraffin blended into resin is an unusually good electrical insulator; 1996, Intel approaches Ajinomoto about developing a film-type insulator using amino acid technology; 1999, ABF ships in Intel's Pentium III, which became the highest-volume CPU on the market within two quarters.
svg.text: From Umami to Substrate
HOW A SEASONING CO-PRODUCT BECAME THE FILM UNDER EVERY AI CHIP
THE SEASONING LINE
Umami is isolated
Kikunae Ikeda traces the taste of kombu broth to one compound: glutamic acid.
AJI-NO-MOTO umami seasoning goes on sale
Ajinomoto crystallizes that glutamic acid into MSG and sells it as seasoning.
Fermentation at industrial scale
Molasses and starch are fed to bacteria that excrete glutamic acid at scale, leaving
co-products such as amino-acid-rich fermentation liquor and chlorinated paraffin.
THE SEMICONDUCTOR LINE
R&D on amino acid chemistry
The Ajinomoto Group begins R&D on applications of amino acid chemistry to
epoxy resins and their composites. Blended into resin, chlorinated paraffin proves
an unusually good electrical insulator, the property ABF would later sell on.
Intel approaches Ajinomoto
Intel approaches Ajinomoto about developing a film-type insulator
using amino acid technology.
ABF ships in Intel's Pentium III
The Pentium III became the highest-volume CPU on the market within two quarters,
taking ABF into mass production.

g.text: Ajinomoto Group, “Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF)” and “Sprinting a marathon” — 1970s research, a 1996 request, adoption in 1999.
Ajinomoto's own account says “a CPU maker approached the Group”; trade coverage names Intel and the Pentium III.
